cards.source_title: Mastra Agents Hour: The Software Factory
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: a "lights-off" version where humans stop reading code entirely
cards.claim: A fully lights-off factory where humans stop reading code quietly rots a codebase after three to six months.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated in episode description; no data given on page, though it follows his year of observation.
cards.landing: Keep human review checkpoints (owner view, Opus reviewer per PR); argues against removing them.

cards.source_title: Mastra Agents Hour: The Software Factory
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Every benchmark rewards one thing: did the test pass?
cards.claim: Coding models are trained only on pass/fail tests and never punished for leaving code a smaller model or later human cannot work in, so slop is structural.
cards.evidence_detail: Argument about training incentives; no numbers.
cards.landing: Verifier design: add maintainability checks beyond tests (import-linter contracts, reviewer rubric); do not trust green CI alone.

cards.source_title: Mastra Agents Hour: The Software Factory
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: why architecture planning, sprint planning, and code review still can't be skipped
cards.claim: Because models are not penalised for slop, architecture planning, sprint planning and code review remain mandatory human/agent steps.
cards.evidence_detail: Conclusion from training-incentive argument; no data.
cards.landing: Ship plan phase routine: keep plan step and per-PR reviewer; argues against skipping them for speed.

cards.source_title: Mastra Agents Hour: The Software Factory
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you're not drowning in PRs so much as drowning in bad ones
cards.claim: The bottleneck is PR quality, not PR volume; the fix is better PRs rather than faster review throughput.
cards.evidence_detail: Episode blurb framing; no numbers.
cards.landing: PR gating: quality of the draft PR body (Plan @ sha, decisions journal) as a filter before review.

cards.source_title: Mastra Agents Hour: The Software Factory
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: a longer-horizon benchmark that actually catches slop
cards.claim: A benchmark that measures code across many successive changes (longer horizon) is needed to catch slop that single-task benchmarks miss.
cards.evidence_detail: Discussed as a wished-for benchmark; no specifics on page.
cards.landing: Measurement idea: evaluate harness changes on multi-phase runs, not single phases (touches the skipped measurement pipeline).

cards.source_title: Beyond Coding ep.270
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Why Coding Agents Keep Making Your Codebase Worse
cards.claim: SlopCodeBench shows AI agents degrade a codebase as features accumulate over time.
cards.evidence_detail: Benchmark across successive features referenced in description; no figures on this page.
cards.landing: Verifier/refuter rubric: check each phase PR for accretive slop; connects to effort-routing report.

cards.source_title: Beyond Coding ep.270
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Why You'll Never One-Shot a Big Feature
cards.claim: Big features cannot be one-shot; they need staged research-design-plan work.
cards.evidence_detail: Timestamp chapter title (00:08:13) only.
cards.landing: Phase routine: one phase per session with explicit plan before implementation; already matches.

cards.source_title: Beyond Coding ep.270
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Why 2-4x productivity beats chasing 100x
cards.claim: Aim for a realistic 2-4x productivity gain rather than chasing 100x dark-factory claims.
cards.evidence_detail: Description and timestamp 00:19:55; no data.
cards.landing: Program expectations: calibrate ship-plan velocity assumptions; not a harness file.

cards.source_title: Beyond Coding ep.270
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Can Deterministic Tools Replace Code Review?
cards.claim: He examines whether deterministic tooling (linters, checks) can replace human code review, alongside the question of dropping pull requests.
cards.evidence_detail: Chapter titles 00:21:31 and 00:24:20 only; his answer not on page.
cards.landing: Backpressure: CI contracts, import-linter, pre-commit gate (a skipped lever); mark as re-opening it.

cards.source_title: Beyond Coding ep.270
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Pull requests, design docs and how engineers build taste now
cards.claim: Design docs and PRs are how engineers keep and build taste when agents write the code.
cards.evidence_detail: Description bullet; chapter 00:27:37.
cards.landing: Plan @ sha draft PR and decisions journal as the taste/design-doc artefact.

cards.source_title: Beyond Coding ep.270
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: one-shots, overnight janitor bots and research-design-plan
cards.claim: His personal workflow combines small one-shots, overnight janitor bots for cleanup, and research-design-plan for big features.
cards.evidence_detail: Description of his own practice; no numbers.
cards.landing: Scheduled routine / janitor agent for cleanup (new custom agent or skill); research-design-plan as skill set.

cards.source_title: Beyond Coding ep.270
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Why Overnight Agents and Heavy Parallelism Backfire
cards.claim: Running agents overnight and in heavy parallel backfires, in tension with his own janitor-bot use; parallelise selectively like poker, not a slot machine.
cards.evidence_detail: Chapter titles 00:38:35 and 00:42:40 only.
cards.landing: Limits on workflow fan-out width and unattended runs; one phase per session.

cards.source_title: Beyond Coding ep.270
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Subscription Maxing vs Paying Per Token
cards.claim: He weighs maxing out flat subscriptions versus paying per token as a cost approach for agent work.
cards.evidence_detail: Chapter title 00:40:10 only.
cards.landing: Cost routing context for effort/model choice; no harness file.

cards.source_title: Beyond Coding ep.270
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Scaling Agentic Engineering to 1,000 Engineers
cards.claim: He discusses how to scale agentic engineering practice across an organisation of about 1,000 engineers, including enterprise friction with background agents.
cards.evidence_detail: Chapter titles 00:05:49 and 00:11:18 only.
cards.landing: Shared reusable skills/agents/workflow library; nowhere obvious beyond that.

cards.source_title: Matt Pocock LIVE: Chat with AI Coding Wizard Dex Horthy
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Understanding LLM Context Windows: Smart Zones, Dumb Zones, and Quadratic Attention
cards.claim: Model quality degrades as context fills (quadratic attention), so work should stay inside the smart zone of the window.
cards.evidence_detail: Podwise summary outline at 08:37; no numbers shown.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md length trim and one-phase-per-session rule; context budget per phase.

cards.source_title: Matt Pocock LIVE: Chat with AI Coding Wizard Dex Horthy
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Task Sizing and Context Management in Ralph for Optimal AI Coding
cards.claim: Task sizing so each loop iteration fits the smart zone is the key to Ralph-style loops.
cards.evidence_detail: Outline entry at 17:07 only.
cards.landing: Phase sizing in ship plan: size each phase to fit a single session's smart zone.

cards.source_title: Matt Pocock LIVE: Chat with AI Coding Wizard Dex Horthy
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Ralph's Refactoring Experiment: Lessons in Codebase Management and Incremental Improvements
cards.claim: He ran a Ralph loop on a refactoring experiment and drew lessons about incremental improvement.
cards.evidence_detail: Outline entry at 24:45; results not shown.
cards.landing: Refactor phases as small incremental loop iterations; nowhere obvious.

cards.source_title: Matt Pocock LIVE: Chat with AI Coding Wizard Dex Horthy
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Integrating Ralph for Issue Triage and the Importance of Trusted Input
cards.claim: Using Ralph for issue triage requires trusted input, since untrusted issue text is an injection and quality risk.
cards.evidence_detail: Outline entry at 32:32 only.
cards.landing: Any automated triage/dispatch agent: gate on trusted inputs; relates to the outbox dispatcher and the defect register.

cards.source_title: Matt Pocock LIVE: Chat with AI Coding Wizard Dex Horthy
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the necessity of human oversight to ensure code quality and alignment
cards.claim: Human oversight is needed for code quality and goal alignment, and classic programming principles give guidance in AI-assisted coding.
cards.evidence_detail: Summary paragraph and outline 44:13 (lead developers, code quality).
cards.landing: Owner view and reviewer steps; classic-principles (small modules) rationale for slice boundaries.

cards.source_title: Matt Pocock LIVE: Chat with AI Coding Wizard Dex Horthy
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Code Layer, an open-source IDE designed to manage parallel cloud code sessions
cards.claim: CodeLayer is an open-source tool for managing many parallel Claude Code sessions, aimed at optimising engineer-AI collaboration.
cards.evidence_detail: Podwise summary of product intro at 05:00.
cards.landing: Session management tooling; harness review skipped context system; nowhere obvious.

cards.source_title: AI Tinkerers One-Shot: How to Ship Complex Features 10x Faster
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: avoiding heavy orchestration frameworks in favor of custom loops built on simple primitives
cards.claim: The most successful enterprise AI teams avoid heavy orchestration frameworks and build custom loops from structured outputs and simple primitives.
cards.evidence_detail: Host summary; he ran his own workflow in production for nine months.
cards.landing: Workflow-tool scripts as plain code; save reusable scripts rather than adopting a framework.

cards.source_title: AI Tinkerers One-Shot: How to Ship Complex Features 10x Faster
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: It structures workflows into discrete steps, integrates with Linear for ticket tracking
cards.claim: Riptide structures Claude Code workflows into discrete steps, tracks tickets in Linear, and stores all artifacts in linked GitHub repos.
cards.evidence_detail: Description of his orchestration tool; nine months in production.
cards.landing: Saved workflow library with artifacts in repo (evidence folders); maps to docs/program evidence.

cards.source_title: AI Tinkerers One-Shot: How to Ship Complex Features 10x Faster
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: serverless GitHub Actions that handle small bug fixes without human intervention
cards.claim: Autonomy comes in levels, from human-in-the-loop review up to GitHub Actions that fix small bugs unattended.
cards.evidence_detail: Description of levels; no numbers.
cards.landing: Scheduled/CI-triggered agent for small defect-register items; deliberately-graded autonomy per phase type.

cards.source_title: AI Tinkerers One-Shot: How to Ship Complex Features 10x Faster
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the engineer's role is now to oversee the entire lifecycle
cards.claim: Engineers now oversee testing, deployment and maintenance like a film producer, since models can code but shipping is the job.
cards.evidence_detail: Host summary of Coding vs Shipping argument.
cards.landing: Closing message six questions and owner view cover shipping lifecycle, not just code.

cards.source_title: AI Tinkerers One-Shot: How to Ship Complex Features 10x Faster
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: “taste” and knowing what not to build the most scarce resources
cards.claim: As code generation accelerates, taste and knowing what not to build become the scarce resources (the infinite software crisis).
cards.evidence_detail: Host summary only.
cards.landing: Plan-review gate where scope cuts are decided; owner decision points in the ship plan.

cards.source_title: Build Wiz AI Show: How to Ship Complex Features 10x Faster
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the power of "tracer bullets,"
cards.claim: Tracer bullets (thin end-to-end slices first) are a way to structure agentic workflows.
cards.evidence_detail: AI-generated feed blurb; no detail.
cards.landing: P1 cold-resume trial as a tracer bullet for the phase routine; thin-slice-first phase design.

cards.source_title: Build Wiz AI Show: How to Ship Complex Features 10x Faster
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: structure agentic workflows that prioritize human design and objective research
cards.claim: Agentic workflows should put human design effort first and use objective research (facts, not opinions) as the input to plans.
cards.evidence_detail: Feed blurb; no detail.
cards.landing: Research step in phase routine that records facts only, separate from plan; knowledge-store of verified diagnoses.

cards.source_title: Build Wiz AI Show: How to Ship Complex Features 10x Faster
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the secret to elite software lies in the "apparatus" you build to orchestrate your AI
cards.claim: Quality comes from the apparatus (harness) built around the model rather than from prompts.
cards.evidence_detail: Feed blurb; no detail.
cards.landing: The harness as a first-class engineered, versioned thing (skills, agents, saved workflows).

gaps: No transcripts obtained for any of the six; I did not attempt YouTube transcript fetches, so every card is read_mode summarised from page descriptions.

LinearB debate page (https://linearb.io/event/the-great-software-factory-debate-2) returned only site navigation; no event content, so no cards from it. Dex's position in the debate (with Aloke Desai, Dan Lines, Andrew Zigler) is unknown. The inventory lists it.
Mastra page says transcript not available; Podwise transcript requires sign-in.
Beyond Coding: only description and timestamps; his actual answers (deterministic tools vs review, PR abolition) are not captured.
Evidence strengths are mostly unknown; SlopCodeBench numbers are not on any of these pages.
